description: US-34 The distribution session is started and ended by hand. THE SOFTWARE DERIVES EVERYTHING FROM THE CALENDAR TODAY: settings hold a week anchor („KW 02/2026 war Rot") and a distribution weekday, and from those follow the eligibility check at the counter, the group tally, the no-show count and the correction window („nur am selben Kalendertag"). THE REAL PROCESS DOES NOT FOLLOW THE CALENDAR — DF merge the two groups for a while, cancel a distribution, hold an extra one — and each time the calendar and the afternoon that actually happened part company: a cancelled Thursday shifts the colour of every week after it as far as the software is concerned, and shifts nothing at all as far as DF are concerned. SO THE BASIS BECOMES THE SESSION THAT ACTUALLY TOOK PLACE: a staff member presses a button to start it, chooses which group(s) it serves (RED, BLUE or both), and presses a button to end it. AT MOST ONE RUNS AT A TIME, the same one on every workstation, and the software NEVER ends one itself — not at midnight, not after a deadline. EVERY HAND-OUT AND EVERY REMINDER BELONGS TO EXACTLY ONE SESSION: „once per calendar day" becomes „once per session", „correctable until midnight" becomes „correctable until the session is ended", and „wrong group" is judged against the RUNNING SESSION'S GROUPS rather than the parity of the calendar week. ENDING freezes the session's hand-outs and writes ONE audit entry carrying the start and the end; a session started by mistake is DISCARDED while empty and leaves NO audit entry at all; the MOST RECENTLY ENDED session can be REOPENED with a reason while no new one has started. A and B OF THE REQUIREMENTS SHIP TOGETHER — without A there is no session for B's hand-outs to belong to, and without B a session is a row nothing reads — which is why this is the largest batch the project has run. THIS BATCH DOES NOT REMOVE THE WEEK ANCHOR: it stops the four rules reading it, and US-36 takes the values out of settings and deletes the arithmetic. Between the two, the settings screen still holds an anchor that only the Start screen's „nächste Ausgabe" line reads — a deliberate intermediate state, one batch long. SCHEMA CHANGE: yes — a new DistributionSession table, sessionId on DistributionRecord and ReminderLog, dayKey and loggedOn REMOVED — so prisma/migrations/ is REGENERATED (pre-release, ADR-009) and THE HAND-WRITTEN PARTIAL UNIQUE INDEX ON Customer.customerNumber MUST BE PUT BACK, alongside a SECOND hand-written index that makes the database refuse a second running session (story 3). BUILD ORDER IS INSIDE-OUT and stories 1–6 must land before any screen story. THE THREE THINGS MOST LIKELY TO GO WRONG: the re-added partial unique index (story 3); the GUARD ORDER in recordAttendance, which US-32.5 documents and which a reordering silently rewords the counter's refusal (story 5); and the TEN EXISTING E2E SPECS that record a hand-out and now need a session started first (story 10). Requirements: local_only/manually-start-ausgabe/refined-requirements.md sections A, B and D-3. Full PRD: tasks/prd-us-34-distribution-session.md

userStories.title: The distribution session is a domain value (domain)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the session's rules — which groups it may serve, which group is proposed next, whether it may be discarded or reopened — in one pure module, so that no screen and no adapter decides any of them. Source: tasks/prd-us-34-distribution-session.md §US-34.1
acceptanceCriteria: NEW module src/domain/distribution/session.ts. PURE: imports nothing from Next.js, React or Prisma, does no I/O, reads no clock (fd/domain-boundary enforces it)

SessionGroups = ReadonlyArray<Group>, made ONLY by createSessionGroups(groups): de-duplicates, orders RED BEFORE BLUE (the order GROUPS in src/domain/customer/group.ts already states and de.customers.list.groupBalance already prints), and throws MissingRequiredField("groups") for an empty set. The TYPE IS THE INVARIANT — a reader may rely on the order and on there being no duplicate, exactly as EggRule works

formatSessionGroups(groups) / parseSessionGroups(stored): comma-separated "RED", "BLUE" or "RED,BLUE". SQLite has no array type; AuditEntry.changedFields already stores a list this way — CITE that, do not re-argue it. parseSessionGroups throws a NEW InvalidSessionGroups(stored) on anything else, because the value re-enters the domain from a column
servesGroup(groups, group): boolean — the one question the counter asks of a session

DistributionSession = { id: number; startedAt: Date; endedAt: Date | null; groups: SessionGroups }, and isRunning(session) is endedAt === null. A DISCARDED SESSION IS NEVER HANDED TO THE DOMAIN — the store filters it out — so there is NO third state here

proposeGroups(lastSession: DistributionSession | null): SessionGroups | null — the group that was NOT up last time; BOTH again when both were; null when no session is on record (the screen renders that as nothing preselected). One line of comment says this is what carries a merged period forward and what stops a cancelled week shifting the cycle; it does NOT re-tell the calendar's story
canDiscard(session, { handouts, reminders }): true only while a RUNNING session holds NEITHER. The counts are passed in — the rule does not know what a hand-out is
canReopen(session, mostRecentlyEnded): true only when session IS the most recently ended one and nothing is running

NEW errors in src/domain/errors.ts in the file's existing shape (readonly code, offending values as readonly fields): InvalidSessionGroups, NoDistributionSessionRunning, DistributionSessionAlreadyRunning, DistributionSessionNotEmpty, DistributionSessionNotReopenable, AlreadyServedInSession, ReminderAlreadyLoggedInSession
AlreadyServedToday and ReminderAlreadyLoggedToday are REPLACED by the last two, not kept beside them — delete them and fix every caller

WRITTEN TEST-FIRST, red → green → refactor, one named test per RULE named after the rule: proposes the group that was not up last time / proposes both groups again after a session that served both / preselects nothing when no session has ever taken place / refuses a session that serves no group / reads a stored RED,BLUE as both groups / refuses to discard a session that has served somebody / refuses to reopen anything but the most recent session
Domain coverage stays at 100%
Full unit suite passes with coverage: npm run test:coverage
Typecheck passes
Lint passes
userStories.notes: First story, src/domain/ only. No schema, no UI, no use case. The judgement call is the group ORDER: RED before BLUE, because GROUPS and the Kundenliste's group balance already read that way — do not invent a second order.

src/domain/distribution/counterVerdict.ts: CounterInput.weekColour: WeekColour becomes sessionGroups: SessionGroups, and servedToday becomes servedInSession

userStories.title: The session table, the port and the adapter (schema + infrastructure)
userStories.description: As DF, I want a started session to survive a restart and a crash, so that a power cut in the middle of an afternoon does not lose which group is being served. Source: tasks/prd-us-34-distribution-session.md §US-34.3
acceptanceCriteria: NEW model DistributionSession in prisma/schema.prisma: id, startedAt DateTime, endedAt DateTime?, discardedAt DateTime?, groups String, @@index([startedAt])

A DISCARDED SESSION IS STAMPED, NEVER DELETED — discardedAt is written and every read filters it out. The model comment says why in two lines: the project deletes nothing (ADR-010) and WaitingListEntry already keeps removed rows for this reason. DF get no paperwork for a misclick because NO AUDIT ENTRY is written, which is a different thing from the row not existing

DistributionRecord GAINS sessionId Int with onDelete: Restrict STATED OUT LOUD, gains @@unique([customerId, sessionId]) and @@index([sessionId]), and LOSES dayKey and @@unique([customerId, dayKey]) — once-per-day is not a rule any more, and a column no rule reads is one a later reader will take for one
ReminderLog GAINS sessionId Int (onDelete: Restrict) and @@unique([customerId, sessionId]), and LOSES loggedOn

AT MOST ONE RUNNING SESSION, ENFORCED BY THE DATABASE. Prisma cannot express a partial unique index, so hand-write it at the END of the regenerated migration beside the one on Customer.customerNumber: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "one_running_session" ON "DistributionSession" ("startedAt" IS NOT NULL) WHERE "endedAt" IS NULL AND "discardedAt" IS NULL; — the indexed expression is constant-by-construction, which is the point: every running row collides

IF SQLite refuses that expression, the fallback is a nullable runningMarker Int? column carrying 1 while running and NULL otherwise with @@unique([runningMarker]), documented as A KEY THE CONSTRAINT NEEDS in the sense Customer.firstNameFolded is one — NEVER as a second answer to 'endedAt IS NULL'. Whichever is used, an integration test proves a second running session is refused
MIGRATIONS ARE REGENERATED, NOT STACKED (pre-release, ADR-009): delete prisma/migrations/, npx prisma migrate dev --name init, then npm run db:reset

RE-ADD BY HAND the partial unique index on Customer.customerNumber at the end of the regenerated migration.sql. Regenerating DROPS it and the slot rule would then rest on application code alone. src/infrastructure/prisma/schema.test.ts catches a miss — run it

NEW port DistributionSessionRepository in src/application/ports.ts, documented ONCE on the port (never again on the adapter): findRunning(), lastEnded(), start(groups, at) — throws DistributionSessionAlreadyRunning, THE ADAPTER IS THE FINAL AUTHORITY exactly as create() is for a customer number — end(id, at), discard(id, at), reopen(id)

DistributionRecordRepository.listForDay(dayKey) becomes listForSession(sessionId); ReminderLogRepository.findOnDay(customerId, loggedOn) becomes findInSession(customerId, sessionId); ReminderLogEntry.loggedOn becomes sessionId. EVERY hand-written fake in src/application/**/*.test.ts gains them in THIS story or the suite does not compile
NEW adapter src/infrastructure/prisma/distribution-session-repository.ts; the record and reminder adapters follow their ports

NEW integration test against a THROWAWAY SQLite FILE in the shape of distribution-record-repository.test.ts: a session round-trips; a second start is refused while one runs; discard hides the row from findRunning and lastEnded; two hand-outs for one customer in one session are refused by the constraint; listForSession returns only that session's rows
src/infrastructure/prisma/test-support.ts clearRegister deletes the new children first, and tests/e2e/seeding.ts releaseNumbers keeps its delete order the schema's relation list

prisma/seed.ts seeds NO session — a register with one already running would put DF in the middle of an afternoon nobody started. prisma/demo-seed.ts seeds ONE ENDED session with a few hand-outs so the demo build has something in it. Both stay idempotent and write no audit entry
npm run build passes after npm run db:reset — the first symptom of schema/database drift is the settings screen reporting that nothing is configured, so open it
Full unit suite passes with coverage: npm run test:coverage
Typecheck passes
Lint passes
userStories.notes: THE ONLY STORY IN THIS BATCH THAT TOUCHES prisma/. Ninth batch to regenerate the migration history: the hand-written partial unique index on Customer.customerNumber MUST be put back, and a SECOND hand-written index arrives beside it. Two port methods change name and shape here, so every hand-written fake changes with them.

userStories.title: Starting, discarding, ending and reopening a session (application)
userStories.description: As DF, I want the four things I can do to a session to be four small use cases, so that each one is guarded where its rule lives. Source: tasks/prd-us-34-distribution-session.md §US-34.4
acceptanceCriteria: FOUR files in src/application/distribution/, one business action each: start-distribution-session.ts, discard-distribution-session.ts, end-distribution-session.ts, reopen-distribution-session.ts — plus read-distribution-session-state.ts answering what the screens need: the running session, the last ended one, and proposeGroups' proposal for the start form
startDistributionSession({ groups }) refuses with DistributionSessionAlreadyRunning when one runs, stamps startedAt from the Clock, and writes NO AUDIT ENTRY

discardDistributionSession() refuses with DistributionSessionNotEmpty when the running session holds a hand-out or a reminder, stamps discardedAt, and writes NO AUDIT ENTRY. The counts come from listForSession and the reminder store, never from a flag

endDistributionSession() refuses with NoDistributionSessionRunning when none runs, stamps endedAt, and RETURNS a SessionSummary { households: number; totalPaidCents: Cents } derived from that session's records. NOTHING about who did NOT turn up is counted or returned

Ending writes exactly ONE audit entry: what: "distribution.session.ended", changedFields: ["startedAt", "endedAt", "groups"], when = the end instant, and why = the machine-written value this log already uses for changes that ask for no reason — e.g. startedAt=<ISO>, groups=RED,BLUE, households=87, totalPaid=43500. A discarded session is NOWHERE in the log, and no session appears in it that began and never ended

reopenDistributionSession({ reason }) requires a trimmed non-empty reason (MissingAuditReason), refuses with DistributionSessionNotReopenable unless the target is the most recently ended session AND nothing is running, clears endedAt, and writes what: "distribution.session.reopened" with the reason as why

TDD against HAND-WRITTEN FAKES, never a mock library. Named tests: refuses a second session while one is running / discards a session nobody was served at / refuses to discard a session that served somebody / counts what was taken when the session ends / writes one audit entry naming the start and the end / writes nothing to the log when a session is discarded / refuses to reopen a session with another one running / refuses a reopening with no reason
Application coverage stays at 100%
Full unit suite passes with coverage: npm run test:coverage
Typecheck passes
Lint passes
userStories.notes: Four use cases, one file each — small, and they share one fake repository, which is why they are one story. The only subtle rule is that START and DISCARD write NOTHING to the audit log: the log never shows a session that began and never ended.

userStories.title: Every hand-out and every reminder belongs to the running session (application)
userStories.description: As DF, I want nothing to be recordable outside a session, so that a booking can never end up belonging to no afternoon. Source: tasks/prd-us-34-distribution-session.md §US-34.5
acceptanceCriteria: recordAttendance loads the running session FIRST and throws NoDistributionSessionRunning when there is none. THE GUARD ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING and its comment is UPDATED, not deleted: session → once-per-session (canRecord) → eligibility (evaluateAtCounter against the session's groups) → the payment. Asked in any other order the counter reads the wrong sentence back (US-32.5)
The record is written WITH sessionId. The price still comes through describeAllowance at the recording instant and the balance is still derived (ADR-015) — neither changes
correctAttendance loads the record's OWN session and refuses with RecordNoLongerCorrectable unless it is running. The error keeps its shape but names the session rather than the day
Removing a hand-out makes the household unserved IN THAT SESSION again, with NO CODE OF ITS OWN: the constraint is (customerId, sessionId) and the row is gone
recordReminder writes sessionId, refuses a second reminder in the same session with ReminderAlreadyLoggedInSession, and refuses outside a session like the hand-out does

lookupCustomer takes the running session, throws NoDistributionSessionRunning when there is none (the screen will not offer the lookup; a hand-typed URL is not the screen's to refuse), and feeds sessionGroups and servedInSession to the verdict
TodaysRecordView becomes SessionRecordView and reminderLoggedToday becomes reminderLoggedInSession. The THREE MONEY FIGURES on it (paidCents, askedCents, balanceWithoutRecordCents) are unchanged
getWeekColour is NO LONGER CALLED BY ANY USE CASE. It survives for the Start screen until US-36 — do not delete it here, and do not add a caller

Application coverage stays at 100%. Named tests: refuses a hand-out with no session running / records against the running session / serves a BLUE household at a session serving both groups / turns a RED household away from a BLUE session / lets a record be corrected while its session runs / refuses to correct a record whose session has ended / allows a household served yesterday to collect at today's session
Full unit suite passes with coverage: npm run test:coverage
Typecheck passes
Lint passes
userStories.notes: This is where the calendar stops deciding anything at the counter. The two traps: the GUARD ORDER in recordAttendance (US-32.5 documents why), and CertificateControls deriving 'expired' from lookupCustomer.customer.certificateExpired rather than from the verdict kind — which must stay true now that ALREADY_SERVED outranks CLEAR_TO_SERVE_CERTIFICATE_EXPIRED.

userStories.title: The group tally follows the session (application)

GroupRosterView.group: WeekColour becomes groups: SessionGroups

The counting rule in src/domain/distribution/groupProgress.ts is UNTOUCHED: a blocked household stays out of the expected count UNLESS it has already collected (a household blocked at three o'clock did collect at two)

Where BOTH groups are served, the tally is read PER GROUP so the screen can state 'Rot: 43 von 60 · Blau: 44 von 60' rather than one merged fraction — the register's own reading, and the one that shows a group falling behind

userStories.title: Starting and ending the session on the distribution screen (presentation)
userStories.description: As a DF staff member, I want to start the afternoon with one press and end it with one, so that the screen says what is happening rather than what the calendar predicted. Source: tasks/prd-us-34-distribution-session.md §US-34.7
acceptanceCriteria: /ausgabe shows, WHILE A SESSION RUNS, a session header stating that one is running and which group(s) it serves, in the place the week-colour banner stood

THE WEEK-COLOUR BANNER IS REMOVED FROM THIS SCREEN IN THIS STORY: on a Tuesday session it would read „Heute ist keine Ausgabe" over a counter serving customers, which is the one plainly false thing the screen could say. Its de.distribution.banner.* keys go with it

The group(s) are NAMED IN WORDS and wear the same badge the Kundenliste and a customer's record wear (GROUP_STYLES, variant="outline") — one colour means one thing application-wide (ui_styling_guide.md §12)

With no session running the screen offers „Ausgabe starten" with a group choice: THREE options — „Rot", „Blau", „Rot und Blau" — as a native radio group, ONE PRESELECTED from proposeGroups, and NONE preselected when there is no session on record
Deviating from the proposal asks for NOTHING: no reason, no confirmation, and NO SENTENCE EXPLAINING THAT IT IS ALLOWED (ui_styling_guide.md §8)

While a session runs the screen offers „Ausgabe beenden", which CONFIRMS in a dialog naming what is being closed: how many households were served and the total taken. The dialog says NOTHING about households that did not turn up — that is the normal case, not a warning
While the running session holds nothing, the screen also offers „Ausgabe verwerfen", which DISAPPEARS the moment the first hand-out or reminder is recorded. It confirms in one dialog
The group(s) CANNOT be changed while the session runs: there is no control for it, and nothing on the screen explains its absence

All German strings live in src/i18n/de.ts under distribution.session; NO German literal enters a component. The verdict wording alreadyServedToday: „Heute bereits ausgegeben" becomes alreadyServed: „Bereits ausgegeben"

userStories.title: Record ADR-020 and update what it makes wrong (documentation)
userStories.description: As the next developer, I want the reason the calendar stopped deciding written down once, so that nobody re-derives it from the code. Source: tasks/prd-us-34-distribution-session.md §US-34.12
acceptanceCriteria: ADR-020 via the record-adr skill: „The distribution session, not the calendar, is what a hand-out belongs to".
